the leucine-responsive protein (Lrp), which is both a transcriptional regulator and a nucleoid-associated DNA-binding protein, binds non-specific DNA with high affinity and that the binding of specific DNA is not significantly more selective than the binding of non-specific sites.

the leucine-responsive protein Lrp does not follow the typical trend of transcriptional regulatory proteins and has a approximately twenty-fold binding discrimination between its specific and non-specific sites.

the leucine-responsive protein Lrp binds DNA with a approximately 20-fold lower affinity to specific DNA sequences than previously thought, that the binding of Lrp to specific DNA sequences is dependent on cooperative binding of Lrp, and that the high affinity of Lrp for non-specific DNA sequences is due to the lack of a specific DNA recognition sequence and to cooperative binding.
